# e Bay Inc (EBAY) Deep Dive Analysis

Report 029 | Published 2020-08-16 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2020-8-16/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/029.json)

Fiscal dependence and e Bay consolidation.

The long-horizon e Bay investment produced solid absolute returns, though below SPY. Its operating turnaround was uneven and the GAAP earnings path failed. The major fiscal compromise came after the election. The dated Bitcoin view succeeded; open-ended gold and valuation views need explicit failure conditions.

**Coverage:** All numbered text blocks and image labels read. Material theses, forecasts and explanations are included; routine holdings lists, incidental statistics, company descriptions and boilerplate are excluded. Chart pixels were not inspected.

## Claims

### 029-C01

**Fiscal transfers sustain consumer income**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Mixed |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | US demand |
| Source blocks | 6, 8, 9, 49, 54, 57, 60, 62 |
| Thesis family | fiscal-income-buffer |

BEA recorded rising transfers and income despite lost employment, supporting the buffer. Currency depreciation is not a mechanical consequence of every fiscal expansion, and simultaneous reopening also affects spending.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.

**Timing:** No fixed endpoint supplied.

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [May 2020 personal income and outlays](https://www.bea.gov/news/2020/personal-income-and-outlays-may-2020) | BEA | 2020-06-26 | Verified in the audit

Personal income fell 4.2% in May after revised 10.8% growth in April. Declining recovery payments explained much of the decrease, partly offset by unemployment benefits. Spending rose 8.2%.

- [June 2022 Consumer Price Index](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/cpi_07132022.htm) | Bureau of Labor Statistics | 2022-07-13 | Verified in the audit

June 2022 headline CPI rose 9.1% over twelve months.

### 029-C03

**PPP maturation explains layoffs**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Mixed |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | US employment |
| Source blocks | 22, 28, 29 |
| Thesis family | ppp-expiry-layoffs |

Some early borrowers reached their initial coverage window, but PPP forgiveness periods were extended and loan maturity was not July. White-collar job loss needs sector flows; a single employer anecdote cannot establish a national credit-cycle cause.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.

**Timing:** No fixed endpoint supplied.

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [PPP Flexibility Act implementation](https://legacy.sba.gov/article/2020/jun/08/joint-statement-sba-administrator-jovita-carranza-us-treasury-secretary-steven-t-mnuchin-regarding-0) | SBA / Treasury | 2020-06-08 | Verified in the audit

Forgiveness covered period extended to 24 weeks; prior borrowers could elect eight weeks. Loan maturity was distinct, generally two or five years, not end-June 2020.

- [July 2020 employment situation](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_08072020.htm) | BLS | 2020-08-07 | Verified in the audit

Payrolls rose 1.8 m in July after 4.8 m in June and 2.7 m in May; unemployment fell to 10.2%. Permanent job losers were approximately unchanged at 2.9 m in July; temporary layoffs fell 1.3 m.
